classification.difficultyReason: Determine two triangular areas from an unlabelled grid, subtract their sum from the whole, and compare shaded and unshaded areas.

content.prompt: In the diagram below, find the ratio of the shaded area to the unshaded area.

spec.description: A square with a visible 4 by 4 grid and two shaded triangles. Free-form TikZ is required because the shading cuts across grid cells along oblique boundaries.
spec.mathematics: Using internal grid-unit coordinates only, the lower shaded triangle has vertices (0,0), (4,0), (2,2); the upper shaded triangle has vertices (2,2), (3,4), (4,4). The diagonal from (0,0) to (4,4) is continuous. No coordinates or numerical labels are printed.
spec.answerVisibility: Both shaded regions and all grid and diagonal boundaries are permanent question givens.

answer.short:
$5:11$

Find the two shaded triangle areas in grid-square units, then subtract their sum from the whole square.
answer.worked:
Take one small grid square as one square unit.

$$\begin{align*}\text{Lower shaded area}&=\frac12\times4\times2=4\\\text{Upper shaded area}&=\frac12\times1\times2=1\\\text{Total shaded area}&=4+1=5\\\text{Unshaded area}&=4\times4-5=11\\\text{Shaded area : unshaded area}&=5:11\end{align*}$$
